canvas-38.description: Sheet 73 of Hudson County Volume 8 covers open ground in the west of North Bergen, between the Westshore Railroad along the top edge and Monroe Street along the bottom. Church Lane crosses the sheet from side to side at about mid-height. On the right half, on both sides of Church Lane, the land is taken up by long glass-roofed greenhouses with their heaters, laid out in rows on narrow lots; this is a nursery district, and the greenhouses carry on from sheet 74 to the right. A small dwelling stands on the south side of the lane, and a few houses and a cow barn with a shed stand in the upper left. Grove Church Cemetery fills the upper right and is shown only as an outline and a lettered name. Most of the left half is unbuilt and carries only property lines and a few lot lines. Along the bottom the north side of Monroe Street is lined with narrow lots numbered in the 700s, mostly with detached frame dwellings, and Maple, Oak, Chestnut and Poplar Streets enter from the sheet below (sheet 75). A north arrow in the upper left points to the upper left; the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 74 to the right, 75 below, and 76 and 77 to the left.
notes: No street junction is drawn on this sheet. It is placed from points carried from sheet 75 (Maple, Oak and Chestnut Streets at Monroe Street) and sheet 74 (the end of a greenhouse), so its position is low confidence.
Church Lane is probably today's 46th Street, inferred from the junction fit of sheet 74; the other streets no longer exist here.
The Westshore Railroad is lettered "WESTSHORE RAILROAD" along the top edge.
Printed sheet 73 of Hudson County Volume 8 (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

canvas-40.description: Printed sheet 74 of Hudson County Volume 8A covers a strip of thinly settled ground in the western part of North Bergen, between Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike), which crosses the top of the sheet, and the sheets of the adjoining district. The sheet is turned on the page: the plank road runs across the top rather than up the side, and the compass at the left shows north towards the upper right. Two streets, 34th and 35th, run down the page between the plank road and Midway Place, with the short West Place branching to the left at the upper block. The streets are lettered 50 feet wide, West Place 10 feet. The blocks are numbered 1 to 4, 7 and 8 and are laid out in narrow lots, with lot numbers 1666 to 1698 and 801 to 855 printed along their fronts. Almost the whole sheet is vacant. The only buildings are a row of about thirteen attached two-storey brick dwellings, shown in pink with house numbers 813 to 839, along the west side of 35th Street, and a group of four more dwellings on West Place. A large unplatted tract fills the left side of the sheet and the lower left corner. Six-inch water pipes are drawn in 34th Street, Midway Place and West Place, and 24, 36 and 30-inch pipes follow the plank road. The neighbouring sheets named on the margins are 72, 73, 75, 78, 82 and 83. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with a scale of feet at the foot.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is today's Tonnelle Avenue.
Old 34th and 35th Streets are today's 79th and 80th Streets on the west side of North Bergen (old number plus 45); the fit against modern intersections is 0.3 m RMSE.
Midway Place follows today's Grand Avenue and West Place today's Liberty Avenue.
The compass shows north towards the upper right (rotation about 64 degrees).
Printed sheet 74 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

canvas-42.description: Sheet 75 of Hudson County Volume 8 shows a belt of built-up blocks at the top and the open Palisade Cemetery grounds below, cut diagonally by the Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike). Monroe Street runs across the top and Main Street across the sheet at about two-fifths of its height. Between them, blocks 11, 12 and 13 are bounded by Maple, Oak, Chestnut and Poplar Streets, which run down the page; the lots are narrow, numbered in the 700s and 900s, and carry detached frame dwellings, a few of brick, and sheds. A scenic painting studio occupies a long building in block 11, beside Oak Street. South of Main Street, block 9 has a row of narrow lots with houses along its frontage. Below that the ground is open: a few houses stand along the turnpike near the left edge, and the cemetery office is the only building of the cemetery shown. The Hackensack Plank Road runs from the upper left to the lower right as a wide street with its name and "Turnpike" lettered along it. The Town of Union boundary is lettered at the lower right. A north arrow at the lower left points to the upper left; the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 73 above, 77 to the left, 76 to the right and Union sheet 40 below.
notes: No street junction is drawn on this sheet. It is placed from two points carried from sheet 76 (the edge of Poplar Street at the Main Street wedge and at the private Monroe block), with scale and north taken from the config; low confidence.
The Hackensack Plank Road is today's Bergen Turnpike, though most of the old line shown here is not a surviving street.
The cross street at the right edge is lettered "MAIN ST." and the main label is lettered "MAIN"; both are the same street.
Printed sheet 75 of Hudson County Volume 8 (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

canvas-44.description: Printed sheet 76 of Hudson County Volume 8A covers a small piece of western North Bergen on the north-west side of Hudson Boulevard West. The sheet is turned on the page, with the boulevard along the bottom and north towards the upper right. Edna Place, a 40 foot street, runs up the page from the boulevard and is crossed by four cross avenues, from the top Kentucky, Maryland, Delaware and Pennsylvania Avenue, each 40 feet wide and lined with six-inch water pipes. Along the left, 39th Street, 45 feet wide, runs up from the boulevard beside a column of narrow lots. The blocks are numbered 5, 6, 8 and 9 north of Maryland Avenue. Settlement is thin: a line of about a dozen detached frame dwellings with house numbers 5 to 37 stands along both sides of Edna Place, with a few dwellings and sheds at the boulevard end, a dwelling near the left of the boulevard and some outbuildings at the right. Most of the ground between 39th Street and Edna Place is unplatted. Lot numbers 1792 to 1821 appear along the cross avenues. Blank ground at the upper left belongs to sheets 77 and 78, and the sheet names 75 and 47 on the left and bottom margins and 81 at the right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a scale of feet at the foot.
notes: Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard; 39th Street is today's 83rd Street.
Edna Place is placed on the modern 85th Street, and Maryland Avenue on Newkirk Avenue; Kentucky, Delaware and Pennsylvania Avenues do not survive. Medium confidence: three control points only.
The compass shows north towards the upper right.
Printed sheet 76 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

canvas-46.description: Sheet 77 of Hudson County Volume 8 covers a part of western North Bergen between Tonnele Avenue on the left and Willow Avenue on the right, with the Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) cutting across the lower left. Four cross streets run across the sheet from top to bottom: Van Wagenen Place, Van Buren Place, Monroe and Main. Between them lie blocks 6, 7 and 8, with narrow lots mostly 25 feet wide and a mixed development of detached frame dwellings, flats, a carpenter's shop, a gypsum shop and a few sheds, some blocks still largely vacant. East of Willow Avenue a second set of blocks, 10 and 14, run along Maple Street, Church Lane and Monroe, with a row of dwellings on the south side of Monroe and Main Streets. At the lower left the Plank Road, with its name and "Turnpike" lettered along it, meets Tonnele Avenue at a water-pipe junction numbered 25. At the top, a block outline belongs to sheet 78, drawn at a turned orientation. A north arrow at the top points to the upper left; the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 78 above, 79 and 80 to the left, 73 and 75 to the right and 85 below.
notes: Tonnele Avenue is today's Liberty Avenue (the modern Tonnelle Avenue lies further west). Main, Monroe, Van Buren Place and Van Wagenen Place are today's 43rd, 44th, 45th and 46th Streets, as on sheet 80 of Volume 8; confirmed by a fit of three junctions on Liberty Avenue at 0.13 m and the atlas scale.
The Hackensack Plank Road is today's Bergen Turnpike.
Printed sheet 77 of Hudson County Volume 8 (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

canvas-48.description: Printed sheet 78 of Hudson County Volume 8A shows the western edge of North Bergen along Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike), which runs up the left side of the sheet with north towards the upper left. Most of the sheet is a large vacant tract, bounded at the top by a diagonal property line that belongs to the neighbouring sheet 77, with a single yellow frame building near the top edge. The built-up part lies at the foot. Two streets, 36th Street and 35th Street, run across the page from the plank road to Midway Place, which runs up the right-hand side, and each is lettered 50 feet wide. Between them is block 5, cut into narrow lots, with a few dwellings, a shed and a small building near the plank road end and two small brick or frame buildings in the middle of the block. The strip between the plank road and the upper block holds block lots along the north side of 36th Street, with a dwelling pair and a single dwelling. Lots to the right of Midway Place belong to sheet 75, and Moore Avenue is lettered at the right margin. Fire hydrants and 24, 36 and 20-inch water pipes are marked beside the plank road, with house numbers 640 to 852 along the two streets. Neighbouring sheets named are 74, 75, 76, 77 and 83. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is today's Tonnelle Avenue; Midway Place follows today's Grand Avenue.
Old 35th and 36th Streets are today's 80th and 81st Streets; fit RMSE 0.55 m on four points, so the placement rests on only two streets.
The compass shows north towards the upper left.
Printed sheet 78 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

canvas-50.description: Printed sheet 79 of Hudson County Volume 8A is the north-western corner of North Bergen, reaching the Bergen County line at the top, where Fairview Cemetery is lettered across the boundary. Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) runs up the left side with north towards the upper left. Three streets, 5th, 4th and 3rd Street, run up the page from Myers Avenue to the county line, and Danielson Avenue, Townsend Street and Flower Street run across below Myers Avenue. The streets are lettered 40 or 50 feet wide, and six-inch water pipes lie in several of them. The upper blocks are laid out in narrow lots with lot numbers 1912 to 1970 and street numbers 760 to 819, but are mostly vacant. Buildings stand in the lower half: a few frame dwellings and sheds on block lots along the plank road, a large unplatted tract with two dwellings and a shed in the middle of the sheet bounded by a slanting line, and a group of dwellings and outbuildings on the east side of 4th and 3rd Streets above Danielson Avenue. A small circular tank is marked beside 4th Street. A dividing line, with Hudson County below and Bergen County above, crosses the top of the sheet. Sheet 77 lies below, 84 to the left and 80 to the right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is today's Tonnelle Avenue; 5th, 4th and 3rd Streets are today's Columbia, Grand and Newkirk Avenues.
Flower, Townsend, Danielson and Myers are today's 88th, 89th, 90th and 91st Streets. Fit RMSE 0.75 m, leave-one-out 1.1 m on nine points.
The county boundary is printed at the top edge.
The compass shows north towards the upper left.
Printed sheet 79 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

canvas-52.description: Sheet 80 of Hudson County Volume 8, lettered North Bergen, shows the western part of North Bergen between the Erie Railroad tracks along the top edge and Tonnele Avenue along the bottom. The sheet is turned on the page, with north towards the upper right, so the numbered cross streets run up the page. The top margin is taken up by the New York Susquehanna and Western Railroad and the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (both Erie Railroad), drawn as parallel tracks, with the compass rose. Below them Dell Avenue crosses the sheet with the Gardner and Rendall Lumber Company yard and a lumber pile on its north side. Van Buren Place, Van Wagenen Place, Church Lane and Monroe Street run down the page from Dell Avenue to Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike), the old turnpike that crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right and meets Church Lane near the right edge. South of the turnpike the blocks end at Tonnele Avenue. The built-up parts are along the turnpike and Tonnele Avenue: frame dwellings, a saloon, a stair builder's shop, a post office, a Roman Catholic church with convent, rectory and parochial school, and the First Baptist Church with its parsonage. The blocks between Dell Avenue and the turnpike are mostly platted lots with few buildings, and several lots carry only foundations or a dwelling to be built. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 20 inches are marked in most streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 79 on the left, 78 on the right and below, 77 at the bottom left and 81 at the right edge.
notes: Old Dell Avenue is today's Dell Avenue; Tonnele Avenue is today's Liberty Avenue, not the modern Tonnelle Avenue, which lies between Dell Avenue and Liberty Avenue.

Monroe, Van Buren Place, Van Wagenen Place and Church Lane are today's 44th, 45th, 46th and 47th Streets (confirmed by the fit to Dell and Liberty Avenues); Hackensack Plank Road here is the stretch now called Bergen Turnpike.
Elm Street and Maple Street are lettered only at the right edge, where they continue on sheet 81.
Printed sheet 80 of Hudson County Volume 8 (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

canvas-54.description: Sheet 81 of Hudson County Volume 8, lettered North Bergen, covers the north-western edge of North Bergen where the West Shore Railroad yards and the Erie Railroad lines pass. The sheet is turned on the page, with north towards the upper left, so the Erie tracks (New York Susquehanna and Western Railroad and Northern Railroad of New Jersey) run up the page along the left edge and Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) runs up the right edge. A curving corridor labelled New Railroad Avenue, formerly Railroad Avenue and now property of the West Shore Railroad, sweeps from the top centre to the lower right with a fan of West Shore tracks beside it; the top of the sheet is marked as continuing on Volume 8A. Along the turnpike at the top are the West Shore Railroad Company's freight buildings: an office, store house, oil house and open platform, a section house and a signal tower, together with the Railroad Y.M.C.A. building. South of the railroad the ground is mostly large unsubdivided tracts. Platted lots lie along Cedar Street and Madison Avenue near the turnpike and between Elm and Maple Streets, with a few frame dwellings, a store room, a carpet cleaning works and several foundations for dwellings. Elm Street is marked not opened and Maple Street is partly not opened. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Sheet 80 adjoins below.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road here is today's Tonnelle Avenue; Maple is today's Aschoff Place; Madison Avenue and Cedar are today's 48th and 49th Streets (confirmed by the fit).
The street lettered Church Lane on sheet 80 is lettered only in part at the lower right corner of this sheet.
Fisher Avenue is cut by the right edge of the sheet; the reading is partial.
Printed sheet 81 of Hudson County Volume 8 (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

canvas-56.description: Sheet 82 of Hudson County Volume 8A covers a long strip of open and lightly built land in North Bergen on the west side of Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike), at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is drawn with the turnpike running up the right-hand edge. Hamilton Avenue, Bair Avenue, Hudson Place and River Street enter the turnpike from the east, and only the first blocks of the neighbouring sheets 74, 73 and 71 show beyond it. Across the left half of the sheet run the parallel tracks of the New York, Susquehanna & Western R.R., the Northern R.R. of New Jersey and the West Shore R.R., side by side down the page. West of the tracks the sheet is blank apart from property lines. Between the tracks and the turnpike lies open ground cut by long property lines, with a few scattered frame dwellings and sheds near the turnpike, and, beside the tracks, the Belmont Stone Co. stone crusher with its stone pockets and concrete buildings. At the foot of the sheet is a small platted block of lots on Grove Street, between the turnpike and the tracks, with frame dwellings, and a street strip lettered River crosses the lower edge, with boat sheds, a silo and the Alexander Gun Club on the far side. Water pipes of 20, 24 and 30 inches are drawn along the turnpike. North is towards the upper left. Adjoining sheets are 83 above, 64 below and 74, 73 and 71 along the turnpike.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is today's Tonnelle Avenue. Hamilton Avenue, Bair Avenue, Hudson Place and River Street meet it where 76th, 74th, 73rd and 69th Streets do (matched by their spacing along the road; fit RMSE 1.6 m, scale 3.79 px/ft). Hudson Place and River Street are not in the reference data as such.
Placed as a four-point similarity along one street (three detected junctions and one hand-picked at Bair Avenue), so its rotation rests on points on one line.
The strip lettered River along the foot of the sheet is read as a street name; only the word River is printed there, and River Street is lettered at the turnpike end.
Printed sheet 82 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

canvas-58.description: Sheet 83 of Hudson County Volume 8A shows the industrial edge of North Bergen along Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike), at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned a quarter turn, so the turnpike runs along the foot of the page with 34th, 35th and 36th Streets opening off its south side. In the upper right is the plant of B. T. Babbitt, Inc., manufacturers of soaps, enclosed by a heavy line: a group of large brick buildings lettered by letter, including the soap, glycerine, potash, rosin, powder and storage buildings, with a boiler reservoir, a machine shop and engine room, fire pumps, a gasoline tank, a suction line from the creek and a lettered note on fire protection, with a small creek running beside the works. Below the plant three railroads run across the sheet from lower left to upper right: the New York, Susquehanna & Western R.R., the Northern R.R. of New Jersey and the West Shore R.R., with Babbitt's Station on the Susquehanna line. A spur of the Public Service Ry. leads to a pair of stone crusher buildings with electric power near the lower middle. The rest of the sheet is open land divided by property lines, with a few sheds and a dwelling near the turnpike. Six inch and larger water pipes are drawn along the works and the turnpike. North is towards the upper left. Adjoining sheets are 84 to the right, 82 to the left and 74 and 78 below.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is today's Tonnelle Avenue. The old 34th, 35th and 36th Streets meet it where 79th, 80th and 81st Streets do (old number plus 45, as on the other sheets west of the boulevard); the lead changed this from plus 46 after review (fit 0.32 m at the atlas scale, against 0.50 m and +0.4 percent for plus 46).
Placed as a three-point similarity along one street, all three junctions detected.
The property lines running diagonally across the open land are not streets.
Printed sheet 83 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

canvas-60.description: Sheet 84 of Hudson County Volume 8A covers the northern tip of North Bergen along the Bergen County line, at 100 feet to an inch. The top edge is the boundary between Bergen and Hudson Counties, lettered with both county names. The only developed edge is on the right, where Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) runs the length of the sheet as a street about 66 feet wide as drawn with Myers Avenue, Townsend Street, Flower Street and State Street entering it from the east. Beyond the road the blocks east of it continue on sheets 79 and 77, and only their edges appear here. The rest of the sheet is open farmland and marsh, without buildings except a single small frame dwelling, divided by property lines and crossed by Belmans Creek, which flows down from the county line and turns toward the southeast. The railroad of the Northern R.R. of New Jersey, four tracks wide, runs down the left side of the sheet. A dash-dot match line of the neighbouring sheet crosses the foot of the sheet. North is towards the upper left, so the road, which runs nearly up the page, bears north-north-east. Adjoining sheets are 83 below, 79 and 77 to the right.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is today's Tonnelle Avenue. Myers Avenue, Townsend Street, Flower Street and State Street meet it where 91st, 89th, 88th and 86th Streets do, confirmed by their spacing along the road (fit RMSE 0.8 m).
Placed as a four-point similarity along one street, so its rotation and scale rest on points all along Tonnelle Avenue.
The creek name is read as Belmans Creek; an apostrophe could not be made out.
Printed sheet 84 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen). This record holds sheets 73-84 of both Volume 8 and Volume 8A (different ground, same numbers); canvas ids keep them apart.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, covers a strip of the Woodcliff district between Bergenline Avenue along the top and Hudson Avenue along the bottom, with Palisade Avenue crossing the middle of the sheet. The cross streets, lettered 29th, 30th, 31st and 32nd Streets, run down the page and are drawn 50 feet wide; Bergenline Avenue is an 80-foot street carrying 36-inch and 8-inch water pipes, and Weatherbee Place enters it from the north at the top. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, with the compass at the top showing north towards the upper right, so the streets run across and down the sheet rather than along its axes. The ground is lightly built up. Most of the blocks are platted into long narrow lots with only a scattering of frame dwellings, some of them with outbuildings, facing the cross streets. The largest works are a long frame building near Bergenline Avenue and 31st Street, drawn with a note that it is dilapidated, with sheds and wagon sheds beside it, and a block of flats in the pink brick tint beside 30th Street. Near the foot of the sheet, on the block between 30th and 31st Streets, stands North Bergen District School No. 2 in brick, and across 31st Street are Grove Reformed Church and the volunteer fire department's engine house, Woodcliff Engine Co. No. 2, with its bell tower. Blocks are numbered 1, 2, 3, 13, 14 and 15. The left edge of the sheet carries the number of the adjoining sheet 34, the right edge sheet 38, with sheets 44 above and 39 below.
notes: Old 29th to 32nd Streets are today's 73rd to 76th Streets (old number plus 44), east of Bergenline Avenue convention verified on sheets 40 and 42.
Weatherbee Place is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and was not used as control.
The junction of 73rd Street and Hudson Avenue was rejected as 10.7 m from the fit; the other nine detected junctions fit to 0.44 m.
Printed sheet 37 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, shows a large undeveloped tract on the west side of the Woodcliff district. It is bounded by Bergenline Avenue, an 80-foot street with 36-inch and 8-inch water pipes, across the top, by 35th Street, a 50-foot street, down the right-hand side, and by a row of platted blocks facing Hudson Avenue along the bottom. Hamilton Avenue enters Bergenline Avenue from the north at the upper left. Almost the whole sheet is a single blank parcel with no streets, lots or buildings drawn, apart from two small frame buildings at the lower middle labelled as a stone shute and crusher, with a smaller engine or boiler building beside them, which probably served quarrying on the tract. The only other buildings are a few dwellings and outbuildings at the upper left, outside the parcel boundary. Along the bottom, blocks numbered 10, 11 and 12 are laid out in narrow lots between 32nd, 33rd, 34th and 35th Streets, with a few frame dwellings and outbuildings on the 32nd and 33rd Street blocks and the rest vacant. Water pipes of 6 inches run in each of these cross streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page with the compass at the left showing north towards the upper right, so Bergenline and Hudson Avenues run across the sheet with a slight tilt. The left edge carries the number of the adjoining sheet 37, the right edge sheet 56, with 44 and 46 above and 40 below.
notes: Old 32nd to 35th Streets are today's 76th to 79th Streets (old number plus 44).
Hamilton Avenue is not used as control. Its junction with Bergenline Avenue lies on the neighbouring sheet area above the drawn blocks.
Control rests on four junctions along Hudson Avenue and one at 35th Street and Bergenline Avenue, so the fit has little cross-wise spread; low confidence.
Printed sheet 38 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, covers the Woodcliff district between Hudson Avenue at the top and Bulls Ferry Road at the bottom, with Broadway, an 80-foot street, crossing the middle of the sheet. Four 50-foot cross streets, lettered 29th, 30th, 31st and 32nd Streets, run down the page and divide it into two rows of blocks, numbered 19, 20 and 21 above Broadway and 29, 30 and 31 below it. Six-inch water pipes run in the cross streets, and twelve-inch and six-inch mains are shown along Bulls Ferry Road. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, with the compass at the right showing north towards the upper right, so the numbered streets run across and down the sheet. The upper row is mostly vacant: blocks 19 and 20 are laid out in narrow lots with only a handful of frame dwellings, and block 21 has a few more dwellings, a barn or shed and a small brick dwelling in pink. The blocks south of Broadway are far more built up. Closely spaced two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings with porches line the 29th, 30th and 31st Street frontages, several brick dwellings and flats are tinted pink in block 30, and a garage, sheds and a two-storey building marked as an office stand near 31st Street and Broadway. The lowest lots of blocks 30 and 31 are still unbuilt strips running back to Bulls Ferry Road. Adjoining sheets are 36 on the left, 40 on the right, 37 above, and 42 and 41 below.
notes: Old 29th to 32nd Streets are today's 73rd to 76th Streets (old number plus 44).
Bulls Ferry Road is today's Park Avenue; Broadway and Hudson Avenue keep their names.
Printed sheet 39 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 of Hudson County Volume 8A covers six blocks of the Woodcliff section of North Bergen, east of Bergenline Avenue and north of the Guttenberg line. The streets drawn are Hudson Avenue along the top edge, Broadway across the middle and Bulls Ferry Road along the bottom, crossed by 32nd, 33rd, 34th and 35th Streets running up the sheet. The old numbered streets are 44 lower than today's, so the sheet runs from modern 76th to 79th Street, and Bulls Ferry Road is today's Park Avenue. The blocks are numbered 22 to 28 and are fully platted into narrow lots of 25 by 100 feet, with house numbers along each frontage. Building is light and almost entirely residential: detached frame dwellings of one, two and two and a half storeys, many with rear sheds and porches, scattered among vacant lots; a few brick or brick-veneered dwellings stand on Broadway near 34th Street. There are no factories, churches or schools on the sheet. Street widths are lettered at the corners, 50 feet for the numbered streets and 80 feet for Broadway, and water pipes and fire hydrants are drawn along Broadway and Bulls Ferry Road. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right, so the numbered streets run up the page and the avenues across it. Adjoining sheets are 38 above, 39 to the left, 41 below and 56 to the right.
notes: Old 32nd to 35th Streets are today's 76th to 79th Streets (old number plus 44).
Bulls Ferry Road is today's Park Avenue.
Printed sheet 40 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, covers the Woodcliff blocks between Bulls Ferry Road along the left edge and the curving line of Hudson Boulevard East on the right, from 30th Street at the bottom to 35th Street at the top. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, with the compass at the upper right showing north towards the upper left, so the numbered streets run across the sheet and Bulls Ferry Road runs up it. Five blocks, numbered 36 to 40, are platted into long narrow lots running back from Bulls Ferry Road, and each block ends at the diagonal frontage of the boulevard in a wedge of shorter lots. Hudson Boulevard East is an 80-foot street, drawn as a wide empty band running from the upper middle to the lower right; the large blank areas to its right belong to the adjoining sheets 49 and 50. Bulls Ferry Road is 80 feet wide and carries 12-inch and 6-inch water pipes, and 6-inch pipes run along the left end of several cross streets. Almost nothing is built: two frame dwellings and a small barn or shed stand near the left end of block 39, and the other blocks show only lot lines. The notes "not opened" are lettered on 30th, 31st and 32nd Streets, where they reach the boulevard. Adjoining sheets are 56 above, 40 to the left, 39 to the lower left and 42 below.
notes: Old 30th to 35th Streets are today's 74th to 79th Streets (old number plus 44).
Bulls Ferry Road is today's Park Avenue; Hudson Boulevard East is today's Boulevard East.

The detector placed 79th Street / Park Avenue about 11 m and 74th Street / Park Avenue about 10 m from the drawn junctions, so both and 79th Street / Boulevard East were excluded; the fit rests on eight junctions along Park Avenue and Boulevard East.
Printed sheet 41 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42, lettered North Bergen and Guttenberg, covers the strip between Bulls Ferry Road (today's Park Avenue) on the left and Hudson Boulevard East on the right, from 26th Street (Hermann Avenue) at the bottom to 30th Street at the top. The dash-dot North Bergen and Guttenberg boundary line runs across the sheet just north of 27th Street (Ferry Road), so the lower third is Guttenberg and the rest North Bergen. Hudson Boulevard East, an 80-foot drive, comes up the sheet from Guttenberg, turns along 27th Street and then runs north up the middle of the sheet before bending east along 30th Street; Bellevue Avenue (1st Street) crosses between 26th and 27th Streets. The Guttenberg blocks along 26th and 27th Streets are the most built up, with frame dwellings, flats, saloons, a bake house and sheds near Bulls Ferry Road, and a scatter of dwellings eastwards. North of the boundary the North Bergen blocks between 28th and 30th Streets are platted but almost empty, with a single dwelling or two, and 28th to 30th Streets east of the boulevard are marked not opened. Large areas east of the boulevard are blank. Water pipes and hydrants are shown on 26th and 27th Streets and on the boulevard. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, with north towards the upper left, so the numbered streets run across the sheet. Adjoining sheets are 41 above, 39 and 36 to the left, 30 below (Volume 8A, West New York) and 50 to the right.
notes: Old 26th to 30th Streets are today's 70th to 74th Streets (old number plus 44).
Bulls Ferry Road (Park Avenue) is today's Park Avenue; Hudson Boulevard East is today's Boulevard East.
Modern Ferry Road meets Bellevue Avenue and Boulevard East at one node near the old 27th Street and Bellevue Avenue corner; the 1910 Ferry Road followed 27th Street (today's 71st Street).
Printed sheet 42 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, covers the west side of the Woodcliff district along Hudson Boulevard West, which runs down the left edge as an 80-foot street with 6-inch water pipes. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, with the compass at the lower left showing north towards the upper left. A band of title lettering and the number of sheet 45 occupy the strip across the top, above Hamilton Avenue, and a separate strip at the foot of the sheet, lettered 31, shows ground continued from sheet 31 with 8th Street, a hydrant, a six-inch pipe and a few buildings. Between the boulevard and 5th Place lies a large tract of lots and open land. At its upper end, along Hagemann Place, which is marked not improved, are a row of small frame dwellings numbered 2 to 16 and 601 to 611, a few pink-tinted brick dwellings near the boulevard, and, nearer Hagemann Place, a frame hall and shed. The lower part of this tract is blank, with a few scattered dwellings and outbuildings. East of 5th Place two long blocks of narrow lots lie between Hamilton Avenue and Weatherbee Place, divided by 4th Place; the block east of 4th Place has a row of nine pink-tinted brick dwellings with stepped fronts, numbered 953 to 975, and the other block is vacant. Below Weatherbee Place a row of narrow lots, a brick building and a frame building stand beside the lower edge of the sheet. The 5th and 4th Place streets are 40 and 45 feet wide. Adjoining sheets are 45 above, 44 to the right, 72 and 70 to the left and 31 below.
notes: Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
5th Place and 4th Place are today's 5th Avenue and 4th Avenue, and Weatherbee Place is today's 74th Street, the westward continuation of old 30th Street across Bergenline Avenue.
Hamilton Avenue and Hagemann Place do not match any modern street line (modern 76th Street lies about 20 m south of Hamilton Avenue and modern 75th Street about 35 m south of Hagemann Place).

Placed from one hand-picked junction (5th Avenue and 74th Street) with scale and rotation from the config; low confidence. Modern 4th Avenue and 74th Street lies 23 m from where the drawn junction falls, so 74th Street was realigned and that junction was not used.
Printed sheet 43 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, covers the Woodcliff blocks on the west side of Bergenline Avenue, with Hamilton Avenue along the top, Weatherbee Place across the middle and Bergenline Avenue, an 80-foot street with 36-inch and 8-inch water pipes, down the right-hand side. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, with the compass at the right showing north towards the upper left, so the avenues run down the page and Weatherbee Place and Hamilton Avenue run across it. Three blocks of narrow lots, separated by the 45-foot streets lettered 3rd, 2nd and 1st Place, lie between Hamilton Avenue and Weatherbee Place. They are moderately built up with closely set two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, mostly facing the east-side streets, with a few sheds, an auto garage, two three-storey buildings near 1st Place and Hamilton Avenue, and scattered vacant lots, especially at the north end of each block. A row of narrow lots south of Weatherbee Place carries several more frame dwellings, and below it a large undivided tract fills the lower half of the sheet, empty apart from a few outbuildings and dwellings near its lower right corner. At the right edge, across Bergenline Avenue, short pieces of 31st and 30th Streets and the corners of the blocks of sheets 37 and 38 are repeated. A band along the foot of the sheet, lettered 32, carries the scale bar. Adjoining sheets are 46 above, 43 to the left, 38, 37 and 34 to the right and 32 below.
notes: 3rd, 2nd and 1st Place are today's 3rd, 2nd and 1st Avenues, and Weatherbee Place is today's 74th Street, the westward continuation of old 30th Street across Bergenline Avenue; old 30th and 31st Streets east of Bergenline Avenue are today's 74th and 75th Streets.
Hamilton Avenue does not match any modern street line near here and was not used as control.

All five control points lie along Weatherbee Place and Bergenline Avenue (four of them on one line), so the fit has little cross-wise spread and the leave-one-out error is large (10 m); the scale and rotation agree with sheets 41 and 43.
Printed sheet 44 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-45.description: Sheet 45 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, covers the north-west part of the Woodcliff district along Hudson Boulevard West, which runs down the left side of the sheet. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, with the compass at the lower right showing north towards the upper left. Hamilton Avenue forms the foot of the sheet, with the number of sheet 43 below it, while 36th and 35th Streets, each 50 feet wide, run across the upper and middle parts. Between them lies block 3, one long block of narrow lots, entirely vacant. South of 35th Street, three blocks numbered 5, 6 and 7 are separated by 5th, 4th and 3rd Places, each 50 feet wide, and are platted for lots with no buildings drawn. Below them a large part of the sheet is an undivided tract. On its west side, between the boulevard and 5th Place, stand several frame dwellings, a shed and two large frame buildings, one marked Training Stable. On its east side, near 3rd Place, is a group of frame buildings marked as greenhouses with glass roofs, with a dwelling and outbuildings, and a few small buildings stand near the lower right. A large blank parcel above 36th Street, with a single building on its upper edge, belongs to the adjoining sheet 47, and narrow strips at the left edge repeat the numbered streets of sheets 75 and 72. The upper left corner carries the sheet number and the heading North Bergen. A six-inch water pipe runs along the boulevard and along Hamilton Avenue and the other numbered streets are marked at 50 feet; Hamilton Avenue is marked 35 feet. Adjoining sheets are 47 above, 75 and 72 to the left, 43 below and 44 to the lower right.
notes: Old 35th and 36th Streets here are taken as today's 79th and 80th Streets (old number plus 44), checked by their distance from Hamilton Avenue and from 3rd, 4th and 5th Avenues; 5th, 4th and 3rd Place are today's 5th, 4th and 3rd Avenues, and Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
Modern 79th Street is an 80-foot street against 50 feet drawn, and modern 80th Street lies about 8 m further from 79th Street than 36th Street is drawn from 35th, so 80th Street was not used.
Placed from one junction (5th Avenue and 79th Street), with scale and rotation from sheet 44; the junction carries about 5 m of uncertainty. Low confidence.
Printed sheet 45 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46, lettered North Bergen, covers the part of the town along the west side of Bergenline Avenue, between Robinson Street at the top and Hamilton Avenue at the bottom. The sheet is turned on the page, with the compass rose at the right edge pointing north towards the upper left, so the numbered streets run across the sheet and Bergenline Avenue, an 80 foot street, runs up its right-hand side. Most of the ground is platted but unbuilt: two large blocks of narrow lots between Robinson Street and 36th Street, and between 36th and 35th Streets, are drawn with lot lines and numbers only, and carry no buildings except a few sheds and dwellings at the Bergenline corner north of 36th Street. South of 35th Street three smaller blocks, separated by 3rd, 2nd and 1st Places (each 50 feet wide), have lot lines at their north ends. Below them a long stretch of open ground, crossed only by property lines, holds a few scattered frame buildings, a shed marked Aeroplane Shed, and an embroidery works with its own steam power and electric light at the corner of 35th Street and Bergenline Avenue. The south end of the sheet along Hamilton Avenue is the most built up, with frame dwellings on narrow lots and, at the Bergenline corner, Marcy's Casino, a large hall with stage and scenery, heated by steam and lit by gas and electricity, with a canvas awning and platform beside it. Water pipes and hydrants are marked on the cross streets. Adjoining sheets are 47 above, 56 to the right above and 38 of the same volume to the right below, and 44 below. A stamp of the Map Division, Princeton University Library, lies over the blank ground.
notes: Old 35th and 36th Streets are today's 79th and 80th Streets (old number plus 44).
1st, 2nd and 3rd Places are today's 1st, 2nd and 3rd Avenues.
Hamilton Avenue lies on the line of today's 76th Street (fitted at 0.4 m residual).
Robinson is printed without a suffix and is not in the modern street network; it is not used for control.
Drawn scale is 50 feet to an inch.
Printed sheet 46 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47, lettered North Bergen, is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with the compass rose at the top pointing north towards the upper right. Bergenline Avenue runs across the foot of the sheet and Hudson Boulevard West across the upper part, and between them lies the west end of the North Hudson Driving Park, the Guttenberg Track, drawn as a long oval with a judges' stand marked inside it. A private driveway bends round the outside of the track from the boulevard down to Bergenline Avenue. Above Hudson Boulevard West a row of platted blocks is bounded by short cross streets: Moore Avenue, 38th Street, 39th Street, Edna Place, State Street and 40th Street, with the page numbers 75, 76 and 81 of Volume 8 marking the sheets that continue beyond them. Most of the ground between the boulevard and the track is open, with a few frame outbuildings and sheds, two larger stable-type buildings beside the driveway, and a row of dwellings and sheds along the boulevard frontage near State Street. At the lower left Robinson Street runs up from Bergenline Avenue beside a block of narrow lots with a few dwellings, saloons and sheds at the Bergenline corner. South of Bergenline Avenue the edge of the next sheet shows a short stretch of 38th Street with a few houses and Overlook Hose Company No. 2. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along the main streets. The adjoining sheets are 46 to the left, 48 to the right, 45 to the left above and 56 below.
notes: Robinson is today's 81st Street at Bergenline Avenue (the same corner is drawn on sheet 46).
Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard; the numbered cross streets above it do not match the modern 82nd to 84th Streets by simple renumbering.
Placed as an anchored part on the 81st Street and Bergenline Avenue junction with the scale of 100 feet to an inch; low confidence.
Printed sheet 47 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48, lettered North Bergen, shows the north-east end of the North Hudson Driving Park (the Guttenberg Track) and the road junctions around it, at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned on the page, with the compass rose at the top pointing north towards the upper right. Bergenline Avenue crosses the foot of the sheet; Hudson Boulevard East leaves it to the south and Bulls Ferry Road runs off to the upper right, with a second street continuing below the crossing. Hudson Boulevard West comes in from the left along the top of the sheet and swings round the end of the track in a long curve to meet Bergenline Avenue, with Bergenwood Road running off east from the top of the curve. Crossley Road and Hoffman Place join the boulevard from the north-west. The boundary between Hudson County and Bergen County is drawn as a dash-dot line down the right-hand side of the sheet, with Probst Street and Lincoln Place stopping at it. The oval of the driving park track is drawn without buildings; the only structures are rows of horse stalls beside the track at the left, a few dwellings, a saloon and shed at the Bergenwood Road corner, The Waldorf with its bowling alleys and a pavilion on the inside of the boulevard curve, a skating rink at the Bergenline Avenue corner, a small oval marked Racer near the county line, and Nungesser's Hotel at the Bulls Ferry Road corner. Water pipes are drawn along the boulevard, Bergenline Avenue and Bulls Ferry Road. Adjoining sheets are 47 to the left, 81 and 80 of Volume 8 above, 56 and 55 below.
notes: Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard and Hudson Boulevard East is today's Boulevard East; they meet Bergenline Avenue at one three-way junction.
The Bulls Ferry Road crossing of Bergenline Avenue is taken as today's Anderson Avenue and Bergenline Avenue; this identification is not confirmed.
Placed from two hand-picked points 70 m apart with the scale of 100 feet to an inch and rotation from the measured lines; low confidence.
Bergenwood Road meeting Hudson Boulevard West is probably today's Bergenwood Avenue and Kennedy Boulevard junction, not used for control.
Printed sheet 48 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 of Hudson County Volume 8A is a 100 ft to an inch sheet of the North Bergen shore of the Hudson River below the Palisades, from the Bergen County line at the top to the foot of 35th Street at the bottom. It is turned on the page, with north towards the upper left. Most of the sheet is open water and blank ground. Along the left edge Hudson Boulevard East runs up from 35th Street through North Hudson Park and meets Bulls Ferry Road, a 25-foot road that climbs in a loop to River Road at the top of the sheet, where the Hudson and Bergen County boundary crosses diagonally. The Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike or River Road runs down the middle of the sheet along the shore, 50 to 66 feet wide. On the river side are a dilapidated pier on solid filling near the county line, several pile piers marked as having no floor, a boat house and floating boat house, and the pier of the Active Boat Club; a cluster of small buildings with a boat shop and dwellings stands on the turnpike, and a few shanties lie on the shore below the park. The land between the boulevard and the turnpike is undivided and unbuilt. Water pipes are drawn along the turnpike. Adjoining sheets are 51 to the left, 56 and 41 on the boulevard side and 50 below.
notes: Hudson Boulevard East is today's Boulevard East; old 35th Street is today's 79th Street; the turnpike is today's River Road.
Placed from two corners carried from sheet 56 (200 ft to an inch): the 35th Street crossing of the boulevard and the fork of Bulls Ferry Road; low confidence.
Printed sheet 49 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 of Hudson County Volume 8A is a 100 ft to an inch sheet of the Hudson River shore below the cliff at the North Bergen and Guttenberg line. It is turned on the page, with north towards the upper left. Hudson Boulevard East crosses the upper left of the sheet, where 31st and 32nd Streets end at it, and bends west at the foot of the cliff; further down, in Guttenberg, the boulevard reappears beside 23rd Street (Ferry Road) and 1st Street, with the curving tracks of the ferry approach. The dash-dot North Bergen and Guttenberg boundary line crosses the lower part of the sheet. The Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike or River Road runs down the sheet along the shore. The only works are the Thiel Contracting Co., dealers in stone and brick, at the top by the shore, and the lumber yard of the Gardner and Meeks Co. at the bottom, with lumber piles and drives on a pier, a lumber shed and a night watchman's clock. The rest of the land between the boulevard and the turnpike is blank, and the river takes up the right side of the sheet. Adjoining sheets are 49 above, 41 and 42 to the left and 26 (West New York) below.
notes: Old 31st and 32nd Streets are today's 75th and 76th Streets; Hudson Boulevard East is today's Boulevard East; the turnpike is today's River Road.
Placed from two junctions only (75th and 76th Streets at Boulevard East), a helmert; low confidence.
Printed sheet 50 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52, lettered North Bergen, is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with the compass rose at the upper right pointing north towards the upper right. It covers the hillside above the Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike, along the Hudson County and Bergen County boundary, which runs as a dash-dot line down the right side of the sheet. Bulls Ferry Road, 33 feet wide, enters at the top left and runs down the left edge. Across the upper part Marks Place, marked not opened, is laid out with long narrow lots; below it Clement runs across the sheet, 50 feet wide, with lots on both sides, and Cedar Avenue and Terrace Avenue come in from the right. The middle of the sheet is crossed by Wall, Lurene and Frances Streets and Valley Road, each 25 feet wide, enclosing a small block, with scattered dwellings and farm buildings at the left. The lower part of the sheet is the built-up edge of the turnpike: Hillside Place and Riverside Place, both 25 feet wide, run up the slope in parallel, joined at the left by Church Street, with rows of frame and brick tenements, dwellings, a saloon, a Standard Oil Company depot and a fire alarm box along them. Hillside Place is marked not opened at its upper end. Along the bottom the Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike, or River Road, 33 feet wide, runs across the sheet with the county line beside it. Adjoining sheets are 54 above, 56 at the upper left, 53 to the left and 51 below.
notes: Placed as a two-point helmert from carried points taken from sheet 54 (Marks Place at Bulls Ferry Road, and Cedar Avenue at the county line); low confidence.

Clement is probably today's Clement Street and Wall is today's Wall Street; the two do not meet on this sheet as the modern streets do, and the modern Valley Road and Wall Street junction was 7.5 m off the carried fit and was excluded.
Bulls Ferry Road is today's Woodcliff Avenue; Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike, River Road is today's River Road.
Lurene and Frances Streets, Riverside Place and Church Street were not found in the modern street network.
Printed sheet 52 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53, lettered North Bergen, is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with the compass rose at the top left pointing north towards the upper right. Its top is North Hudson Park. Hudson Boulevard East, an 80 foot drive, curves in from the left edge and sweeps up the sheet to meet Bulls Ferry Road, which runs off to the upper right edge. Wall Street, also called Dyer's Lane, leaves Bulls Ferry Road at the junction and runs down and to the right towards Clement Street at the right edge. At the left of the boulevard stands Public School No. 1, a brick school heated by steam, with its bell on the lot. The middle of the sheet is open land crossed by lot lines, with a few dwellings, a shed and a barn near Bulls Ferry Road. Along the bottom the Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike, or River Road, runs from the lower left to the right edge beside the Hudson County and Bergen County boundary line. Church Street climbs the slope from the turnpike and turns along the top of a block of narrow lots. The Sacred Heart Roman Catholic Church and a parochial school stand above Church Street, near an outline marked fire ruins, and tenements, saloons, flats and a fire department house with an engine house fill the turnpike frontage. Water pipes of 8 and 12 inches follow the boulevard and the turnpike. Adjoining sheets are 56 above and to the left, 52 at the right, and 51 at the left below.
notes: Wall Street was also called Dyer's Lane; it survives as Wall Street.
Hudson Boulevard East is today's Boulevard East and Bulls Ferry Road is today's Woodcliff Avenue; Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike, River Road is today's River Road.

Placed as an anchored part on the Wall Street and Bulls Ferry Road junction (one detected point, scale 7.56 px/ft from the config); low confidence, the modern Woodcliff Avenue line is a few metres off the drawn road.
Church Street is not in the modern street network under that name.
Printed sheet 53 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54, lettered North Bergen, is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with the compass rose at the upper left pointing north towards the upper right. It shows the strip of the town along the cliff road, Bulls Ferry Road, which runs up the left side of the sheet, and the streets laid out from it towards the east: Palisade Plaza at the top, then Baar Place, New York Avenue, Palisade Avenue and Marks Place at the foot. Kamp Place joins New York Avenue and Palisade Avenue, and Hudson Place runs down the right-hand side. The dash-dot line between Hudson County and Bergen County crosses the sheet from top to bottom near the right. The blocks between Baar Place and New York Avenue are laid out in long narrow lots, many of them still empty, and Baar Place and Marks Place are marked not opened. Buildings are mostly frame dwellings with a few stores: a saloon and a drug store along Palisade Plaza, Castellano Flats and a hall on Bulls Ferry Road, a row of dwellings along New York Avenue and Kamp Place, and the River View Hotel on Palisade Avenue near the county line. A fire bell and a hydrant stand near Palisade Plaza. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches follow the main streets. The numbers of adjoining sheets shown are 55 above, 56 to the left and 52 below, with an edge strip of Cedar Avenue at the lower right.
notes: Baar Place is today's Barr Place; the Palisade Plaza, New York Avenue, Palisade Avenue, Kamp Place and Hudson Place names survive.
Bulls Ferry Road is today's Woodcliff Avenue; its modern line is a few metres off the drawn road, so its junctions were left out of the fit.
Marks Place and Palisade Avenue was detected as a junction at a lot line and excluded; Marks Place is drawn not opened.

Placed from three detected junctions (Hudson Place and Palisade Plaza, Kamp Place with New York Avenue, Kamp Place with Palisade Avenue), an exact fit of low confidence; the fitted scale is 7.57 px/ft against 7.55 expected.
Printed sheet 54 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55, lettered North Bergen, is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with the compass rose at the top right pointing north towards the upper right. It covers the cliff-top amusement ground and road junctions where Bergenline Avenue, Hudson Boulevard East and Bulls Ferry Road meet, east of the North Hudson Driving Park. Bergenline Avenue, 80 feet wide, crosses the upper part of the sheet from the left to the lower right, ending at the junction with Hudson Boulevard West at the right edge. Hudson Boulevard East curves in from the left, a broad drive 80 feet wide, and sweeps round to join Bulls Ferry Road at the right. Bulls Ferry Road runs diagonally up the sheet from the lower left to the upper right edge, where it is crossed by the dash-dot boundary line between Hudson County and Bergen County. The buildings are concentrated beside the boulevard bend: a carousel works marked Fred. Dolle Carousel and Organ Manufacturer with a restaurant and stove-pipe chimneys, an open platform with swings and an ice cream stand, a pool and a small photograph building, a saloon building, a long horse shed, and an incline marked The Tickler. West of the boulevard are scattered dwellings, a shed and Villa Robinson. South of Bulls Ferry Road, Heindel Avenue and Hudson Place are laid out with narrow lots and marked not opened, and the street railway right of way and Palisade Plaza run down the lower left. Water pipes of 6, 8, 12 and 36 inches follow the main roads. Adjoining sheets are 48 above, 56 on the left, 54 below and 52 and 53 beyond.
notes: Bulls Ferry Road is today's Woodcliff Avenue on this stretch; Hudson Boulevard East is today's Boulevard East and Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard.

Placed as an anchored part on one hand-picked point, the Palisade Plaza and Bulls Ferry Road crossing taken as today's Palisade Plaza and Woodcliff Avenue junction, with scale 7.56 px/ft and rotation from sheets 54 and 56; low confidence, 55 has no detected junctions because the cross streets are drawn as not opened.
Woodcliff Avenue lies a few metres off the drawn Bulls Ferry Road on neighbouring sheets, so the point may be off by that much.
Printed sheet 55 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56, lettered North Bergen, is a reduced-scale key sheet drawn at 200 feet to an inch, covering the ground around North Hudson Park between Bergenline Avenue at the top and the Hudson River at the bottom. It is turned on the page, with the compass rose at the lower right pointing north towards the upper right. Bergenline Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, with 35th, 36th and Robinson Streets entering it from above and a short length of 38th Street leaving it below; a note directs the reader to sheet 47 for detail. The long street down the left edge is 35th Street, crossed by Hudson Avenue, Broadway and Bulls Ferry Road. Hudson Boulevard East leaves Bergenline Avenue at the upper right, runs down the sheet beside the park and bends east along the cliff to meet Bulls Ferry Road, on which the cross streets Palisade Plaza, Baar Place, New York Avenue, Palisade Avenue, Marks Place and Wall Street are lettered; a note refers to sheet 53 for detail. A street railway trestle and right of way crosses the park in yellow and curves up to Hudson Boulevard East. Buildings are drawn only at a few places, such as a small group at 38th Street and a pink building near the boulevard. At the bottom Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike, or River Road, runs along the shore of the Hudson River, with three piers drawn in blue, and a second Bulls Ferry Road branches from the boulevard down to it. The sheet carries the numbers of the surrounding sheets of the volume, including 46, 47, 48, 38, 40, 41, 49, 51, 53, 54 and 55.
notes: Old 35th and 36th Streets are today's 79th and 80th Streets, and Robinson Street is today's 81st Street.
Hudson Boulevard East is today's Boulevard East; Bulls Ferry Road on the left side is today's Park Avenue, and on the cliff side its line is today's Woodcliff Avenue.
The drawn scale is 200 feet to an inch, which agrees with the fitted scale of 1.89 pixels per foot.
The 79th Street and Bergenline Avenue crossing on the north-east side (modern node with Riverview Drive) was 8 m from the fit and was not used.
Printed sheet 56 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, covers a strip of Fisher Avenue on the west side of North Bergen, between the Flower Hill Cemetery to the north and the West Shore Railroad to the south. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, with north towards the upper left, so Fisher Avenue runs across the sheet from left to right. The street is a 40-foot way, and along its north and south sides stand rows of narrow lots with frame dwellings, most of them two stories, with a few sheds, a storage building and a small group of flats near the lower right corner. Two cross streets are drawn, 2nd Street and 1st Street, and 5th Street runs parallel to Fisher Avenue below it at the right edge, serving a short row of flats and dwellings. Stanton Street is laid out as a 35-foot street across the northern lots, with only lot lines and no buildings. The upper half of the sheet is blank except for the cemetery lettering and the dividing lines of the plots; the lower half, between the south row of lots and the railroad, is also blank, apart from a pink-coloured building and two yellow buildings at the left edge and a few siding tracks. The West Shore Railroad crosses the bottom as a group of parallel lines, and the foot of the sheet carries the note See Volume Eight. Adjoining sheets are 59 to the left, 58 to the right and 62 above.
notes: Fisher Avenue is today's 51st Street; 1st Street is today's Smith Avenue and 2nd Street today's Durham Avenue (checked against the junctions, which fit at under 1 m on the neighbouring sheet 59).
Newkirk Avenue and Meadowview Avenue, which cross modern 51st Street in this stretch, are not drawn as streets on this sheet.
Placed only from the Fisher Avenue junctions with 1st and 2nd Streets, which lie close together on one street, so scale and rotation are weakly constrained.
Printed sheet 57 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, lies along the eastern boundary of the town, where Hudson Boulevard West is the North Bergen and West New York boundary line. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned, with north towards the upper left, so the boulevard runs diagonally from the top left to the lower right. Fisher Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet and meets the boulevard at 7th Street on the West New York side; 5th Street, which bends near the centre, runs parallel below it, and 1st Street comes in from the left edge. Both Fisher Avenue and 5th Street are lined with narrow lots carrying frame dwellings, flats and a few pink-coloured buildings, with a fire department building of the Peerless Hose Company No. 3 at the corner near the boulevard. In the upper part of the sheet are an embroidery factory with a row of dwellings along the street lettered New, a large group of greenhouses with glass roofs, a fire house and a saloon beside the boulevard, and open ground with Flower Hill Cemetery at the upper left. The West Shore Railroad appears at the lower left, and the centre line of its tunnel crosses the lower part of the sheet. 9th Street and Arthur Place are shown on the West New York side of the boulevard. The sheet is marked See Volume Eight at the foot, and adjoins sheets 57 to the left, 62 above and 1 and 3 across the boulevard.
notes: Fisher Avenue is today's 51st Street; 5th Street is today's 50th Street and 9th Street today's 52nd Street (old number plus 44 east of the boulevard, matched by position).
Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard. The drawn boulevard is wider than the modern road and its modern centre line lies up to 4 m from the junctions detected here.
Only three control points: two junctions with the boulevard and the Fisher Avenue and 1st Street corner, whose street centre lies half off the left edge.
Printed sheet 58 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, covers the industrial and residential district between the Hackensack Plank Road (the Turnpike) at the top of the sheet and the foot of the Palisades on the left, where the lettering along the left edge reads West Shore. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned so that Fisher Avenue runs up the page and 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets run across it. The west part holds a group of large pink-coloured mill buildings, among them the Peerless Rubber Manufacturing Company, a building lettered Mutual Risk Mill Construction, the works of Gellen and Company, manufacturers of chemicals, the Marbleloid Company, lessee, making composition flooring, and the Richard Meyer buckskin tannery, with reservoirs, a tiling room, a cement mixing house and tracks of the West Shore Railroad on the left. East of Fisher Avenue lie blocks of frame dwellings and flats, Public School No. 3 and a few saloons, becoming open lots towards the bottom, where Stanton Street is marked not opened. A railroad station is shown near the top. At the top a break with See Volume Eight marks the edge of the volume, and a vacated railroad avenue is lettered near the upper right. Sheet 60 adjoins above and to the right, 57 below, and 62 to the right.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is today's Tonnelle Avenue; Fisher Avenue is today's 51st Street; 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets are today's Grand, Columbia and Liberty Avenues; North is today's 52nd Street and Williams today's 53rd Street (all confirmed by 0.2 to 0.9 m residuals).
Williams Street (53rd Street) junctions with Tonnelle Avenue and Grand Avenue were rejected at 9.5 m and 8.3 m, so the drawn street may differ from the modern line.
New R.R. Avenue, lettered at the top left, was read from the overview-size crop and is medium confidence.
Printed sheet 59 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, follows the Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike), which runs up the sheet from the bottom to the top. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned, with north towards the upper left. The 50-foot Plank Road is lined on its west side with deep lots holding a few frame dwellings, a saloon and a transformer station of the Public Service Corporation on its east side. Washington Street and Williams Street run east from the Plank Road near the lower part of the sheet and Malone's Lane, a 23-foot lane, runs west from it higher up. At the lower left is the West Shore Railroad round house, a semicircular building of yellow and pink shading with an engine house, and several parallel tracks of the railroad run along the left edge. An office building stands at the foot of Railroad Avenue, lettered as vacated. East of the road, across the upper and right parts of the sheet, is the blank ground of Hoboken Cemetery, with a few dwellings and a cement block making shop near Washington Street. Fifth Street runs south from Williams Street at the lower right. The lower left is marked See Volume Eight. Adjoining sheets are 59 below, 61 on the left and 62 above and on the right.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is today's Tonnelle Avenue; Williams is today's 53rd Street, Washington today's 54th Street and Fifth Street today's Liberty Avenue.

Placed from two hand-picked junctions on the Plank Road and one detected junction on Williams Street; an exact fit with no redundancy, low confidence. Its scale (7.3 px/ft) is about 3 percent below its neighbours.
Malone's Lane and Railroad Avenue (vacated) have no modern counterpart.
Printed sheet 60 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-65.description: Sheet 65 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, covers a long strip of the east side of the town along Hudson Boulevard West, the line between North Bergen and West New York. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper left, so the streets run up and down the page. From left to right are Liberty, Newkirk and the boulevard, crossed at the top by Pierce Avenue and at the bottom by Spring, and with John Street meeting Pierce Avenue from the north at the top. Liberty and Newkirk each break and shift sideways near the lower third of the sheet. The blocks are lined with narrow lots carrying many frame dwellings, with flats, stores, a hall and Dewey Hall, bakeries, a bake house and several saloons facing the boulevard, and sheds in the back lots. Pink and blue-coloured buildings are scattered through the blocks. West of Liberty the lots are mostly empty, and the lower left belongs to the cemetery of Flower Hill, lettered along the bottom. A 6-inch and a 36-inch water pipe run along Pierce Avenue and the boulevard, and 17th Street is marked in West New York at the upper right. Adjoining sheets are 66 above, 63 on the left, 62 below and 5 across the boulevard.
notes: Pierce Avenue and 17th Street are today's 61st Street; Spring is today's 58th Street; Liberty is today's Meadowview Avenue; Newkirk keeps its name; Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard (fit at 0.46 m RMSE).
The 36-inch water main shown at left, running diagonally across the lots, is not a street.
Printed sheet 65 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-66.description: Sheet 66 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, lies at the south-eastern corner of the town where Hudson Boulevard West crosses from the lower left to the lower right as the North Bergen and West New York boundary. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned, with north towards the upper right, so Liberty and Newkirk run across the page and Pierce Avenue, which becomes 17th Street, runs down the left edge. The upper part consists of blocks between Liberty, Newkirk and Pierce Avenue, with frame dwellings on narrow lots in rows near the street line and open lots in the middle. John Street runs diagonally from Pierce Avenue to the right, between Newkirk and the boulevard, and carries a triangular block of dwellings, flats and stores with a printer, a carpenter shop and a blacksmith, a blue-coloured building and a fire department building of the American Hose Company. New Durham Avenue and Robert cut off the right edge, where dwellings of two and three stories with pink-coloured shading face Robert. Washington runs along the foot of the sheet at the left, and 18th Street and 17th Street meet the boulevard in West New York at the bottom. Adjoining sheets are 65 on the left, 67 on the right, 63 and 64 above, and 7 and 5 on the other side of the boulevard.
notes: Pierce Avenue and 17th Street are today's 61st Street; 18th Street is today's 62nd Street; John Street is today's Durham Avenue; Robert is today's 63rd Street; Newkirk keeps its name; Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
The junction at 18th Street and the boulevard was rejected at 12.7 m: the modern boulevard has been realigned there.
Printed sheet 66 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-67.description: Sheet 67 of Hudson County Volume 8A, lettered North Bergen, covers the north-western side of Hudson Boulevard West, on the line between North Bergen and West New York. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned, with north towards the upper left, so that the three avenues New Durham, Smith and Bergenwood run up the page, crossed by North, South and Robert. The blocks are largely filled with frame dwellings of one and two stories on narrow lots, with scattered sheds and stores, Public School No. 5 in the block between Robert and South, a bakery at the boulevard corner, a hall, an auto shop and a few pink-coloured buildings. The land at the upper left, beyond New Durham Avenue and above North, is thinly built. Bergenwood Avenue meets the boulevard at its lower end in a wedge-shaped block; the boulevard runs diagonally up the right edge with its dash-dot boundary line between North Bergen and West New York, and 21st Street, 18th Street and Washington Street are marked on the West New York side. A 6-inch water pipe runs along the avenues and streets. Adjoining sheets are 66 below, 64 on the left, 68 above, and 7 and 9 across the boulevard.
notes: Robert is today's 63rd Street and South is today's 64th Street; New Durham Avenue is today's Durham Avenue; Smith and Bergenwood Avenues keep their names; Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard (fit at 0.94 m RMSE).
North, the northernmost cross street drawn here, has no matching modern street in the reference extract and was not used as control.
Printed sheet 67 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-68.description: Sheet 68 of Hudson County Volume 8A covers the east edge of North Bergen along West Hudson Boulevard, on the line between Guttenberg and West New York. The boulevard runs diagonally down the right side of the sheet, with the boundary line between the municipalities lettered along its centre and 26th Street crossing it at the top and 23rd Street at the foot. West of it the sheet is mostly open ground. The upper half is Rock Cellar Park, with a large dance pavilion, several lettered outbuildings, a wagon shed, a bowling alley with a saloon and a small club building. The lower half holds two blocks of narrow platted lots between Nott Street, Ridgley Street and the boulevard, bounded below by Towerhill Avenue. These carry about thirty detached frame dwellings, some brick or stone-faced, with a few flats, saloons and a concrete building. Below Towerhill Avenue a further block between Smith Avenue and the boulevard holds an embroidery factory with electric lighting, steam heat and water pails, and several dwellings marked as drawn from plans. Along the foot run North Street, labelled not opened in part, New Durham Avenue and Bergenwood Avenue. The drawing is at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, about 33 degrees from vertical. Large white areas to the left belong to the neighbouring sheets 64 and 69. Adjoining sheets are 69 above, 67 below, 64 to the left and 31 and 9 across the boulevard.
notes: West Hudson Boulevard is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard.

The drawn streets in the lower blocks (Smith Avenue, Bergenwood Avenue and New Durham Avenue) correspond to the modern Smith, Bergenwood and Durham Avenues; the lettered North Street is taken as modern 67th Street, which is drawn here only about 17 feet wide.
Nott Street, Ridgley Street and Towerhill Avenue have no modern equivalent.
Street names read from the sheet overview; not all checked on full-resolution crops.
Printed sheet 68 of Hudson County Volume 8A (North Bergen).

sheet-69.description: Sheet 69 of Hudson County Volume 8A lies on the west side of Hudson Boulevard West at the line between North Bergen and Guttenberg, west of the boulevard and north of the ground drawn on sheet 68. The boulevard runs along the foot of the sheet, rising to the right, with the municipal boundary and a six-inch water pipe lettered along it. Most of the left and centre of the sheet is empty ground of large undivided tracts, with only a few small buildings, among them a pair of dwellings near the middle and a cluster near the boulevard at the lower left. At the top left are Lincoln Street and Liberty Street, with a row of dwellings, and Cottage Place runs across the head of the sheet. On the right side Kelly's Lane runs up from the boulevard and a second lane parallel to it, whose name is cut by the margin, runs up the sheet; between them and to their right lies a block of narrow lots with dwellings, and Centre Street crosses at the lower right. The compass shows north to the upper right, and the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. sheet-70.description: Sheet 70 of Hudson County Volume 8A covers a strip of North Bergen west of Hudson Boulevard West, between Cottage Place at the top and the boulevard at the foot. The boulevard runs along the bottom of the sheet, rising to the right, and Hagemann Place meets it at the lower right corner. The sheet is mostly large undivided tracts. A row of narrow lots lies on both sides of Kiesel Street across the middle, with a few dwellings, and McDonald Lane, marked private, runs across below them. The Old People's Home stands in the lower centre, drawn in pink as a two and a half storey building with steam heat, electric light and fire pails. To its right is the plant of the C. F. Mueller Company, makers of macaroni, a three storey building with a drying range, with night watchman, fire pails, electric lights, steam and coal fuel listed. There are some greenhouse-like sheds and a few dwellings at the lower left. Cottage Place and Bair Avenue, the latter marked not opened, are at the top, with a match line between points A and B joining the sheet to sheet 71. The drawing is at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Adjoining sheets are 71 at the top left, 73 above, 72 to the right, 69 to the left and 43 across the boulevard.
notes: Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard; Hagemann Place meets it where modern 74th Street does, and Cottage Place is near modern Cottage Avenue.

sheet-71.description: Sheet 71 of Hudson County Volume 8A covers the west part of North Bergen along Hackensack Plank Road, a turnpike that runs up the left edge of the sheet. Bair Avenue, marked not opened, crosses the head of the sheet. Below it two blocks of narrow lots lie between Hudson Place, Park Place and Richmond Place. The upper left block carries a row of two and a half storey dwellings fronting the turnpike and a few more on Park Place. Across the middle is a large vacant tract and a long range of greenhouses with glass roofs. Lower down are Pierce Street, Hill Road and Ferry Road, which meets River at the foot of the sheet, with a hotel with a saloon on the turnpike, and scattered dwellings and sheds. On the right side Jefferson Street runs up the sheet from the junction at Lincoln, and Liberty Street and two streets named Lincoln cross it, with lots and dwellings on both sides. The compass shows north to the upper left, and the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Neighbouring sheets are 73 at the top, 82 to the left across the turnpike, 70 and 69 to the right and 64 below. A dash and dot match line lettered A and B runs down the right edge.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) is probably modern Tonnelle Avenue.
