sheet-72.description: Sheet 72 of Hudson County Volume 8A shows the west side of Hudson Boulevard West at Woodcliff, where it runs up the right of the sheet. Two cross streets, 35th Street at the top and 34th Street below it, reach the boulevard. Narrow lots about twenty five feet wide are platted on both sides of 34th Street and beyond 35th Street, with only a few dwellings and one small office, so the area is mostly vacant. Below that lies a large unsubdivided tract with a farm house and sheds, and a nurseryman's greenhouses with a boiler house. Hamilton Avenue crosses the sheet near the foot, with a lamp post and house numbers along it. Below it, McDonald Lane, marked private, runs south past the National Cigar Box Company, a works with a pump, electric light and heat, and storage, labelling and printing rooms, and a second range of greenhouses stands to its right. Kiesel Street is at the lower left, and Hagemann Place meets the boulevard across it at the bottom right. The boulevard is drawn 80 feet wide with six-inch water pipes. The compass shows north to the upper left, and the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 75 at the top, 74 and 73 to the left, 70 below and 45 and 43 across the boulevard.

Hamilton Avenue lies close to modern 76th Street, as on sheets 46 and 82 (canvas-56); Hagemann Place is near modern 75th Street.

sheet-73.description: Sheet 73 of Hudson County Volume 8A covers a large block of undeveloped land in North Bergen between Hackensack Plank Road at the top and Hamilton Avenue on the right. Hackensack Plank Road, the turnpike, runs across the top of the sheet, with a hydrant and the lettered pipes of 24 inch, 36 inch and 20 inch mains in the top right corner. Bair Avenue, marked not opened, runs down the left edge, and ends at a lane; at the left edge are also the ends of Park Place and Richmond Place. Hamilton Avenue is drawn 30 to 33 feet wide, running down the right of the centre of the sheet and bending near the foot. The tract between them is undivided and blank apart from a few dividing lines. A small group of buildings, two dwellings and a shed, stands near the foot with a line dividing the lots. Kiesel Street is at the lower left. The area to the right of Hamilton Avenue is also open, with only a few lot lines. The drawing is at 50 feet to an inch. The compass shows north to the upper right. Adjoining sheets are 82 above across the turnpike, 71 to the left, 74 to the right and 70 and 72 below.

Hamilton Avenue is taken as modern 76th Street and Bair Avenue as 74th Street, as on sheet 82 (canvas-56) and sheet 46; the lead moved the anchor from 75th to 76th Street, which closes a one-block gap to sheet 74.

sheet-74.description: Sheet 74 of Hudson County Volume 8 lies on the north-west side of Hudson Boulevard West, which forms its right edge and the boundary with the Town of Union. Church Lane crosses the sheet from left to right at about mid-height and meets the boulevard. North of the lane the ground is largely open: Grove Church Cemetery, a plot of narrow lots along the top edge below the centre line of the West Shore Railway tunnel, and the Grove Reformed Church with its Sunday school and a small shed. South of the lane the sheet is divided into blocks by Danielson Street and Brown Street, which run down the page and are crossed by the narrow Mark Lane. The blocks are dominated by florists' greenhouses with glass roofs and heaters, along with scattered frame dwellings, a shirt factory with a gas engine, and a few sheds. A set of greenhouses at the lower right stands beside the boulevard. The right edge shows the first blocks of the Town of Union, with Fulton, 3rd and 4th Streets meeting the boulevard. The boundary line is lettered along the boulevard. A north arrow in the upper right points to the upper left; the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 73 to the left, 76 below, and Union sheets 42 and 47 beyond the boulevard.
notes: Church Lane is today's 46th Street, Danielson is Smith Avenue and Brown is Bergenwood Avenue; the match was made from the junction fit.
Mark Lane is drawn much narrower than modern 45th Street, so its junctions with Danielson and Brown were hand-picked and are less certain than the others.
Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard. Fulton, 3rd and 4th Streets in the Town of Union are today's 45th, 47th and 48th Streets.

sheet-75.description: Printed sheet 75 of Hudson County Volume 8A shows a stretch of Hudson Boulevard West in the western part of North Bergen, with four streets running up the page from the boulevard: 35th Street at the left, Moore Avenue, 38th Street and 39th Street. The sheet is turned on the page, with the boulevard along the bottom and north towards the upper right. Lots on 35th Street and Moore Avenue are narrow, with a few frame dwellings and a wagon shed near the boulevard end of the block between them. The wide central block between Moore Avenue and 38th Street is mostly vacant but holds the larger industrial buildings: a machine shop with a power plant note (no power, cement floor) and a pair of large frame sheds drawn in yellow, with scattered dwellings at the south edge. East of 38th Street the block carries North Bergen Public School No. 9, a brick building shown in pink and lettered as heated by steam and lighted by electricity, with a few small frame buildings and lots along the boulevard. Street widths are lettered 50 feet for 35th Street, 70 feet for Moore Avenue and 38th Street (the figures are partly cut), 45 feet for 39th Street and a wide Hudson Boulevard West; six-inch water pipes run along the boulevard. House numbers on the boulevard run from 5461 to 5507. Neighbouring sheets named are 72, 74, 76, 78, 45 and 47. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
Old 35th, 38th and 39th Streets are today's 80th, 82nd and 83rd Streets; Moore Avenue is today's 81st Street. Spacing along the boulevard matches the modern nodes within about 15 feet.
36th Street is lettered at the foot of the sheet in the margin belonging to sheet 45.

sheet-76.description: Sheet 76 of Hudson County Volume 8 lies along the west side of Hudson Boulevard West, the boundary with the Town of Union, from Morgan Street at the foot of the sheet to John Street near the top. The upper part of the sheet shows the blocks east of Poplar Street, which runs down the left edge: the private Monroe Street, with narrow lots and dwellings, and the plant of the North Hudson Manufacturing Company, makers of sash, doors and blinds, with sheds and a lumber shed. Below it a row of greenhouses stands on the north side of Main Street, which widens and bends diagonally across the sheet to meet the boulevard. South of that, Hillside Place is lettered as not opened, and a band of lots runs along it. The North Bergen Township Hall, a large brick building, stands on the boulevard. The lower two-thirds of the sheet is open ground belonging to Palisade Cemetery, with the works of the New York and New Jersey Crematory Company in the middle and a few sheds at the bottom. Along the right edge the Town of Union blocks are cut by John, Main, Liberty, Humboldt and Morgan Streets. A north arrow at the right points to the upper left; the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 74 above, 75 to the left and Union sheets 40 to 42 across the boulevard.
notes: Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard. Humboldt, Liberty and Main Streets in the Town of Union are today's 41st, 42nd and 43rd Streets; Morgan Street is 40th Street.

sheet-77.description: Printed sheet 77 of Hudson County Volume 8A covers a platted but almost unbuilt district in the north-west corner of North Bergen, along the east side of Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike), which runs up the left side of the sheet. North is towards the upper left. Three avenues parallel to the road, Michigan, Kansas and Kentucky Avenue, are crossed by State Street through the middle of the sheet, Edna Place near the foot and Flower Street at the top, with a street lettered Easy running up between Flower and a jog in the grid. The blocks are numbered 11 to 17 and are divided into narrow lots, some laid across the block and some along it. Streets are lettered 40 feet wide and carry six-inch water pipes; large mains of 24, 36 and 20 inches follow the plank road. Only a few buildings are shown: two dwellings in pink on State Street in block 15 and two yellow frame buildings on the large vacant tract at the lower left, which a diagonal line cuts off from the platted blocks. The streets at the foot of the grid stop at the edge of this tract, and the right margin shows the lots of sheet 81. Adjoining sheets named are 76, 78, 79, 81 and 84. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with a scale of feet at the foot.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is today's Tonnelle Avenue; Michigan, Kansas and Kentucky Avenues correspond to Liberty, Columbia and Grand Avenues.
State Street is today's 86th Street, Edna Place 85th Street and Flower 88th Street; Easy survives as Easy Street at 88th Street. Fit RMSE 1.2 m on eight points.
88th Street at Columbia Avenue was rejected at 9.5 m: the grid north of the diagonal is offset from the modern streets.

sheet-78.description: Sheet 78 of Hudson County Volume 8 is drawn turned about 90 degrees from its neighbours, with north towards the upper right. It covers the area north of Van Wagenen Place and west of Willow Avenue: block 5, bounded by Tonnele Avenue, Church Lane, Willow Avenue and Van Wagenen Place, holds a row of frame dwellings on the Church Lane and Van Wagenen Place frontages and some vacant ground. East of Church Lane, Madison Avenue runs down the page between narrow blocks lettered A and B, with scattered dwellings, sheds and a small cement-block building. The upper half is occupied by the greenhouses of Herman Schölzel, florist: long glass-roofed houses with heaters, plant beds and a drive between two ranges. The Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) runs along the top, with Cedar Street entering from the north. Jackson Place, a private street, and a lot with a dairy and a storage building for excelsior lie near the right edge, next to the tracks of the West Shore Railroad, which is lettered along the right margin together with a note to see another volume. A north arrow at the upper left points to the upper right; the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 81 above, 80 to the left, 77 below left and 73 below.

sheet-80.description: Sheet 80 of Hudson County Volume 8A covers a block of northern North Bergen along the Bergen County line, just east of the Hackensack Plank Road district and west of Hudson Boulevard West. The top edge is the Bergen and Hudson County boundary line, with Fairview Cemetery lettered in Bergen County above it. Below the line the sheet is laid out in long blocks between 3rd, 2nd and 1st Streets, which run up the page, and Myers Avenue and Danielson Avenue, which cross them. Bergenwood Road runs down the right side of the sheet as a lettered 40 foot street, with Crossley Road entering it from the east and Hudson Boulevard West curving across the lower right corner. Hoffmann Place, marked Not Opened, is a 40 foot street laid out across the lower blocks. Most of the ground is platted into narrow lots but is still vacant, especially along the top of the sheet; building is concentrated in the blocks between Myers and Danielson Avenues, where small frame dwellings stand on the lots, and a few larger frame buildings and a shed stand near Bergenwood Road and on Hoffmann Place. Street widths of 50 and 40 feet are lettered at the corners and six inch water pipes are drawn along the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page: the streets run diagonally against north, with north towards the upper left. Adjoining sheets are 79 to the left and 48 to the right, and sheet 81 lies below.
notes: Myers Avenue is today's 91st Street and Danielson Avenue is 90th Street; Hoffmann Place (not opened) lies along the line of 89th Street.
3rd, 2nd and 1st Streets are today's Newkirk, Durham and Smith Avenues, confirmed by the junction spacing and the fit (0.5 m RMSE).
Bergenwood Road corresponds to the modern Bergenwood Avenue; Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard.

sheet-81.description: Sheet 81 of Hudson County Volume 8A shows a platted but thinly built tract of North Bergen along the north side of Hudson Boulevard West. Four parallel 40 foot avenues, Kentucky, Maryland, Delaware and Pennsylvania, cross the sheet and are cut at right angles by State Street, which runs up the page from Hudson Boulevard West. The blocks, numbered 1 to 10, are divided into narrow lots, with the lot and house numbers lettered along the frontages. West of State Street, the block between Maryland and Delaware Avenues holds a row of eight identical pink-coloured brick dwellings, each lettered Concrete Partition, and two more brick dwellings stand in the block below; a few frame dwellings stand near the lower left corner and along the Boulevard. Most of the other lots are vacant. East of the platted blocks the sheet is open ground with a handful of scattered frame dwellings and sheds, crossed by property lines, and Flower Street is lettered as an unbuilt 40 foot street at the top right. Hudson Boulevard West runs across the foot of the sheet and a 40th Street opens off its south side, with a scale bar and the adjoining sheet number 47 below. Six inch water pipes are drawn along the avenues. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, so that the avenues run across it with north towards the upper right. Adjoining sheets are 77 above, 76 to the left and 80 to the right.
notes: Hudson Boulevard West is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard.

The old avenues appear to survive as Grand, Newkirk, Durham and Smith Avenues (Kentucky to Pennsylvania), judging by the position and spacing of the blocks, but they are not tied to the reference data and State Street is not a modern street north of the boulevard.
The south side of the sheet shows 40th Street at the point where modern 85th Street meets the boulevard; the old street names east and west of the boulevard are not the modern numbering.

sheet-82.description: Sheet 82 of Hudson County Volume 8, lettered North Bergen, shows the Homestead district around the junction of Secaucus Road and Paterson Plank Road in the western part of North Bergen. The sheet is turned on the page, with north towards the upper left. Down the left edge run the New York Susquehanna and Western Railroad and the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (both Erie Railroad), with a switch tower and Homestead Station. Secaucus Road crosses the sheet from the railroad at the left to Tonnele Avenue at the right, and Paterson Plank Road leaves it at a fork near the railroad and runs down the page to Homestead Place. North of Secaucus Road, Washington and Garden Streets, both marked not opened, run up the page between lots, and Tonnele Avenue runs obliquely up to the right edge, where Elm Place joins it. The built-up blocks are along Secaucus Road and Paterson Plank Road: bowling alleys, a saloon, a carriage shop, lumber and horse sheds, a grain and feed warehouse, an ice house, frame dwellings and the Homestead Hose Company No. 3 house. Prospect Avenue and Northern Avenue are marked not opened, as is Homestead Place at the bottom. Large areas of the upper part are unplatted or laid out in empty lots. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches follow the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 83 above, 86 at the right, 88 below and 101 at the left.
notes: Secaucus Road is today's Union Turnpike and Tonnele Avenue is today's Liberty Avenue; Elm Place is today's 38th Street.
Garden may be today's Tonnelle Avenue where it meets Union Turnpike; the modern node sits about 7 m from the drawn street.

sheet-83.description: Sheet 83 of Hudson County Volume 8, lettered North Bergen, lies in the western part of North Bergen between the Erie Railroad and Tonnele Avenue. The sheet is turned on the page, with north towards the upper right. Across the top the New York Susquehanna and Western Railroad and the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (both Erie Railroad) are drawn as parallel tracks, with a section house between them and the compass rose above. Dell Avenue runs across the sheet below the tracks. Anderson Place and Doremus Place run down the page from Dell Avenue to Tonnele Avenue, which crosses the bottom of the sheet obliquely and is met there by Elm Place and Linden Street from the south. The built-up area is two blocks of narrow lots along Anderson Place and Doremus Place, with frame dwellings, a few stables and sheds, a shop and the Nonpareil Roofing Company's tar roofing works near Dell Avenue. A large part of the sheet to the left is unplatted ground with a house and a shed, and Washington Street and Garden Street are lettered along the left edge, where the sheet joins sheet 82. Water pipes of 6 inches are marked in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 82 at the left, 79 at the right, and 85 and 86 below.
notes: Tonnele Avenue is today's Liberty Avenue; Dell Avenue is unchanged; Elm Place, Linden Street, Anderson Place and Doremus Place are today's 38th, 39th, 40th and 41st Streets (confirmed by the fit).

sheet-84.description: Sheet 84 of Hudson County Volume 8, lettered North Bergen, shows the part of North Bergen at the boundary with the Town of Union where Secaucus Road leaves Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike), with Weehawken Cemetery on the right. The sheet is turned on the page, with north towards the upper right. The turnpike crosses the lower part of the sheet from the lower left to the right edge and carries the dash-dot North Bergen and Town of Union boundary line along it. Secaucus Road runs up the page from the turnpike, curves to the upper left and meets Monument Road near the top, where the school stands. Union Place runs up the page at the left, lined with small frame dwellings and flats on narrow lots, with a print shop, a stable and a blacksmith near the turnpike. Between Union Place and Secaucus Road are the Summer Garden with a dancing pavilion and bowling alleys, a saloon and flats, and Public School No. 6. Elm Place and Linden Street appear at the top, and Lewis Street and Gardner Street run south from the turnpike into the Union sheets 39 and 40. Weehawken Cemetery fills the right of the sheet and is unmarked inside. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 86 above, 85 at the right, 95 at the left and 39 and 40 below.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road here is today's Bergen Turnpike; Union Place, Lewis Street, Gardner Street, Elm Place and Linden Street are today's 37th, 38th, 39th, 38th and 39th Streets (Elm Place and Linden Street are the northern ends of 38th and 39th).
Monument Road is today's Grand Avenue, which is drawn about 10 m from the modern line; Secaucus Road is today's Union Turnpike.
The Union Turnpike junction with Bergen Turnpike was left out of the fit because the drawn junction lies about 19 m from the 39th Street corner against 11 m on the modern map.

sheet-85.description: Sheet 85 of Hudson County Volume 8, lettered North Bergen, lies on the boundary of North Bergen and the Town of Union, west of Weehawken Cemetery. The sheet is turned on the page, with north towards the upper right. Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) crosses from the lower left corner, where the North Bergen and Town of Union boundary line is lettered, and curves up to the right edge. Monument Road, which becomes Willow Avenue to the east, crosses the middle of the sheet from the left edge, with Linden Street, Anderson Place and Doremus Place running up the page from it to Tonnele Avenue at the top. The left side holds a block of narrow lots with an embroidery factory with electric motor, a saloon, a dairy with sheds and a cow shed, and frame dwellings, and the F. R. Austin and Brother lumber, sash and door works with its kiln, lumber sheds and warehouse. Clarence Bruce, manufacturer of novelties, stands south of Willow Avenue, and dwellings, one damaged by fire, are scattered along the turnpike. The lower left is the large unmarked area of Weehawken Cemetery. East of Doremus Place a block of lots holds a saloon and a beer garden, and fan-shaped lots with dwellings lie between the turnpike and Tonnele Avenue. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are 83 above, 86 at the upper left, 84 at the left, 79 and 77 at the right and 75 below.
notes: Tonnele Avenue is today's Liberty Avenue; Monument Road and Willow Avenue are today's Grand Avenue; Linden, Anderson Place and Doremus Place are today's 39th, 40th and 41st Streets (confirmed by the fit).
Hackensack Plank Road here is today's Bergen Turnpike.
